body:
National Quantum Mission: approval, period and aims

On 19 April 2023, the Union Cabinet approved the National Quantum Mission (NQM), with a total outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore for 2023–24 to 2030–31. It is an 8-year national programme to strengthen research, technology development and India's quantum-technology ecosystem. Quantum communication is one of its 4 major areas; the others are quantum computing, quantum sensing and metrology, and quantum materials and devices.

The mission's principal quantum-communication targets include satellite-based secure communication between ground stations across a range of 2,000 km within India, as well as inter-city QKD across 2,000 km using existing optical fibre and trusted nodes. It also seeks capabilities for quantum networks and long-distance international quantum communication. These are programme objectives, not claims that every link had already been built by the date of approval.

The 4 thematic hubs

In 2024, the mission established Thematic Hubs (T-Hubs) hosted by major institutions to coordinate work in separate quantum fields.

Quantum technology areaLead institution
Quantum computingIISc Bengaluru
Quantum communicationIIT Madras with C-DOT
Quantum sensing and metrologyIIT Bombay
Quantum materials and devicesIIT Delhi

These institutional assignments are easy to confuse. IIT Delhi participated in specific DRDO quantum-communication demonstrations, but the NQM Quantum Communication T-Hub is hosted at IIT Madras in association with C-DOT.

Important 2025 achievements

17 April 2025: C-DOT and Sterlite Technologies reported an Indian QKD demonstration over 4-core multi-core optical fibre. It showed a way to support quantum-key transmission alongside conventional optical traffic; the milestone concerned a type of fibre, not a new satellite link.

16 June 2025: DRDO and IIT Delhi demonstrated entanglement-based free-space quantum-secure communication over more than 1 km at the IIT Delhi campus. This was an atmospheric optical link, different from their 2022 inter-city fibre demonstration.

5 November 2025: The Department of Science and Technology reported that QNu Labs, with support from the Indian Army and its Southern Command, had demonstrated a QKD network spanning more than 500 km using existing fibre infrastructure in the Rajasthan sector. The route included trusted nodes; it was a network demonstration, not a single direct 500 km photon link.

Prelims focus

  • NQM: approved 19 April 2023; outlay ₹6,003.65 crore; period 2023–24 to 2030–31.
  • Communication goals: 2,000 km satellite-based secure communication and 2,000 km inter-city fibre QKD.
  • Quantum Communication T-Hub: IIT Madras with C-DOT.
  • June 2025: DRDO–IIT Delhi, more than 1 km entanglement-based free-space demonstration.
  • November 2025: QNu Labs and Army-supported fibre QKD network, more than 500 km, with trusted nodes.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, Cabinet Approves National Quantum Mission, 19 April 2023; Department of Science and Technology, DST's Key Achievements During 2024, Thematic Hubs section; Press Information Bureau, C-DOT and STL Achieve India's First QKD over Multi-Core Fibre, 17 April 2025; Press Information Bureau, DRDO and IIT Delhi Demonstrate Quantum Entanglement-Based Free-Space Quantum Secure Communication, 16 June 2025; Press Information Bureau, Startup Supported by DST under NQM Demonstrates 500 km Quantum-Safe Network, 5 November 2025 (accessed 5 November 2026).]

title: National Quantum Mission and Major Developments Through 2025

body:
A reported 1,000 km network milestone

On 8 April 2026, the Government of India reported that a 1,000 km quantum-secure communication network had been demonstrated under the National Quantum Mission using indigenous technology developed by QNu Labs. A further government statement on 30 September 2026 described this as progress towards the mission's 2,000 km communication target.

The reported distance describes a network-level achievement. It should not be interpreted as proof that photons travelled through one uninterrupted 1,000 km fibre section. Similarly, the announcement did not mean that the whole 2,000 km mission target had been completed.

QKD can work together with conventional quantum-resistant security

On 31 August 2026, C-DOT unveiled 14 indigenous quantum-security products covering QKD and post-quantum cryptography. The announcement illustrated how the two approaches can coexist; it was an unveiling, not a claim that every product had entered nationwide operation.

On 30 September 2026, a National Quantum Mission update reported a hybrid PQC–QKD link demonstrated by a team from the IIT Madras Quantum Communication Hub over 17 secure nodes between Chennai and Bengaluru using existing BSNL fibre. The use of both approaches is consistent with their different purposes: quantum-assisted key establishment and mathematically quantum-resistant cryptographic protection.

Gandhinagar's 5.56 km free-space field trial

During the night of 27–28 September 2026, QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar demonstrated a 5.56 km free-space QKD link between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar. The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology announced the trial on 3 October 2026. BISAG-N is the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics.

In the trial, QKD-generated keys were integrated with BISAG-N's Vedic Kavach platform, which incorporated post-quantum cryptography, to encrypt and decrypt test messages. The release described this as India's first free-space QKD demonstration at the 5.56 km scale. It must not be read as India's first free-space QKD experiment of any distance: SAC Ahmedabad had already demonstrated 300 m links in 2021 and 2022.

Gujarat therefore has 2 distinct centres of importance in these milestones: Ahmedabad, through SAC and PRL in the 2021–2022 300 m demonstrations, and Gandhinagar, through the BISAG-N–IIT Gandhinagar 5.56 km field trial in 2026. The cities, institutions, dates and distances should not be interchanged.

Status as of 5 November 2026: The 1,000 km network and 5.56 km Gujarat link were reported demonstrations; the 2,000 km inter-city and satellite-communication figures remained mission targets in the cited government documents. A test of a ground-to-ground free-space link is not a demonstration of satellite QKD.

Prelims focus

  • April 2026: QNu Labs, reported 1,000 km quantum-secure network milestone.
  • August 2026: C-DOT unveiled 14 QKD and PQC products.
  • September 2026: IIT Madras-led hub reported a hybrid PQC–QKD link between Chennai and Bengaluru over 17 secure nodes.
  • 27–28 September 2026: QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar, 5.56 km free-space QKD field trial; announced 3 October 2026.
  • Trap: The Gujarat 5.56 km field trial was neither a satellite link nor India's first free-space experiment at any distance.

[Sources: Press Information Bureau, National Quantum Mission Achieves 1,000-km Secure Communication Milestone, 8 April 2026; Press Information Bureau, C-DOT Unveils 14 Indigenous Quantum Products, 31 August 2026; Press Information Bureau, India's Emerging Quantum Ecosystem Strengthened, 30 September 2026, IIT Madras hybrid-link section; Press Information Bureau, India's First 5.56 km Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated, 3 October 2026; ISRO, Department of Space Demonstrates Entanglement Based Quantum Communication over 300m Free Space, 27 January 2022 (online sources accessed 5 November 2026).]
